PauseAm: Ask before you pay. A voice-first payment decision companion for Nigerians.

drafts.field: Why did you choose this problem statement?
drafts.answer: Payment requests in chats can leave students, everyday users and small businesses uncertain about what to verify. PauseAm tests whether short, practical actions are more useful than a general fraud chatbot. PS2 offers a route to help through Nigerian speech on ordinary phones. This need remains a hypothesis: 200+ people are willing to test, but discovery and documented user validation have not yet been completed.

drafts.field: Describe the artefact you are building (or have built)
drafts.answer: PauseAm is a mobile payment companion with English voice/text questions, bank-first reporting guidance and scam lessons. Official Nigerian-accented-English weights transcribe speech on our SecretVM; users correct and confirm the transcript. The live N-ATLaS CPU model checks retrieved card relevance; actions come from reviewed sources. Six genuine HTTPS model requests passed in 6.1-6.8 seconds. The owner confirms the full voice journey. Public checks passed 20/21; vague changed-bank-details wording safely abstained. These are engineering checks, not participant validation. Users review and send report drafts themselves. No funds are moved, accounts authenticated or recovery promised. Secrets stay server-side; raw audio is not retained by default. Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo are paused; official API and fine-tuning are unverified. The public app/repository exist. Official-ASR-service qualification, 50 documented interactions and the real demo video remain pending.
React/TypeScript, Vinext/Vite, Workers/D1; Python/FastAPI, Transformers/PyTorch ASR; pinned N-ATLaS/llama.cpp Q4_K_M CPU runtime.

PS2: Describe the end-to-end user journey, from voice input to service delivered
drafts.answer: Current English flow: choose a payment question; consent to microphone use; record, listen or discard; separately consent to processing; convert to bounded mono 16 kHz WAV; send server-side to the authenticated official-model host; verify exact model identity and privacy; show the transcript for correction and confirmation; return a short reviewed action checklist. A genuine owner transcript is evidenced; this is not participant validation. Typed source guidance works. The live N-ATLaS CPU relevance service passed six genuine HTTPS requests in 6.1-6.8 seconds. The owner confirms the full English journey; 20/21 public checks passed, with safe abstention for a vague question. It selects only an allowed reviewed card, never model-written contacts or arbitrary safety prose. Failures offer an honest retry/text route, without simulated output. Bank-first report guidance appears immediately; a redacted draft stays in the browser for user review and sending. Learning uses dated, manually maintained official notices. No raw audio retention, PINs, OTPs, passwords, full credentials, safe verdicts or recovery promises. Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo are paused. Organiser acceptance of self-hosted official ASR weights remains unresolved; official API and fine-tuning are unverified.

drafts.field: PS2: User-acquisition plan for reaching 1,000 users within 3 months of award
drafts.answer: The reported 200+ people are prospective willing testers, not existing users. The owner will coordinate discovery and at least 50 consented, observed English voice interactions after the live build passes. If results support the companion, projected post-award acquisition is 200 completed users in month one, 300 additional users in month two and 500 more in month three through student/small-business partners and voluntary educational sharing. These figures are targets, not traction. Measure completion, comprehension, failures and return use without saving private questions or credentials. Expansion to paused languages requires compute and fluent review. Preserve the conservative shared rolling licence guard and obtain separate licensing before exceeding 1,000 active users in a rolling 30 days. Proposed sustainability is sponsored/B2B distribution and support, with the first consumer action free; willingness-to-pay and pricing remain unvalidated.
